title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program — Billing Units Carried by a Model Change Authorization Grant (Reimbursement and Billing Manual)
content:
## Section: billing units on a grant recorded for a CGM model change

Under the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program, when Larkfield records the authorization grant for a new written order of the CGM supply allowance (A4239) that changes the CGM model, under the payer authorization already in force, the billing units that grant carries are fixed by this section. One billing unit of A4239 is one 30-day supply of sensors.

### Clause 1 — formal statement

1.1 **The records read.** The order is the newest written order of the item; the payer authorization is the authorization grant the program's latest refill of the item drew on, and its units left are the units it authorized less the units of refills of the item drawn on it, never below zero; that authorization is a per-period approval when its units equal the whole 30-day blocks of its span, both dates counted, times the tier's allowance per 30 days; the latest refill is the latest refill shipment of the item, read for its ship date and supply days. Here the item is the CGM supply allowance; the newest written order is the one with the latest order date; the payer authorization is the grant recorded on that latest refill shipment; its span runs from its valid-from date through its valid-through date; and the tier's allowance per 30 days is the tier's sensor allowance units per 30 days of supply.

1.2 **The grant's span.** The grant is valid from the order date through the earlier of the payer authorization's valid-through date and the order's valid-through date.

1.3 **The standard grant.** The standard grant carries, for each whole 30-day block of its span, both days counted, the billing units per 30 days written on the order, less one block for each whole 30-day block of the latest refill's supply, its ship date plus its supply days, that runs past the order date. Read in record terms:
- the days of the span are the calendar days from the order date through the grant's valid-through date, both of those days included (none when the valid-through date falls before the order date), and the standard count of blocks is those days divided by 30, any remainder of fewer than 30 days dropped;
- the latest refill's supply ends on its ship date plus its supply days, and the days by which it runs past the order date are the calendar days from the order date to that end (none when the end does not fall after the order date); the standard deduction is one block for each whole 30 of those days, any remainder dropped, and a program with no refill shipment of the item deducts no block;
- the standard grant is the standard count of blocks less the standard deduction, multiplied by the billing units per 30 days written on the order.

1.4 **How the grant is settled.** Each adjustment to the grant changes the standard grant as that adjustment states, in this order: replacements of a standard count, deduction or quantity first, then blocks taken off, the blocks being settled before they are multiplied by the units per 30 days; the grant carries a whole number of units, never below zero.

### Clause 2 — the same rule set out as inputs and outcome

| Element | Where it is read | How it enters the standard grant |
|---|---|---|
| Order date, quantity per 30 days, order valid-through date | the newest written order of the CGM supply allowance | start of the span; billing units per block; one candidate end of the span |
| Payer authorization valid-through date | the grant the latest refill shipment drew on | the other candidate end of the span; the earlier end governs |
| Ship date and supply days | the latest refill shipment of the CGM supply allowance | end of the supply already shipped; whole 30-day blocks past the order date are deducted |
| Billing units carried | — | blocks of the span less blocks deducted, multiplied by the billing units per 30 days written on the order, a whole number never below zero |

### Clause 3 — worked figures on hypothetical inputs

The figures below are illustrative only, in a hypothetical non-leap year, and carry no program value.

*Hypothetical case A.* Suppose an order dated 1 March writes 2 billing units per 30 days and is valid through the last day of the following February; suppose the payer authorization is valid through 31 August, and the latest refill shipped on 15 February with 60 days of supply.
- Span: 1 March through 31 August (the earlier of the two valid-through dates), 184 days both counted; 184 divided by 30 gives 6 whole blocks, 4 days dropped.
- Supply end: 15 February plus 60 days is 16 April, which runs 46 days past 1 March; 46 divided by 30 gives 1 whole block deducted.
- Units: 6 blocks less 1 deducted block leaves 5 blocks, multiplied by 2 units per 30 days, gives **10 billing units**.

*Hypothetical case B.* Suppose the same order, but the payer authorization is valid through 19 April and the latest refill's supply runs 75 days past 1 March. The span is 50 days, giving 1 whole block; 75 days give 2 whole blocks deducted; 1 block less 2 deducted blocks is below zero, so the grant carries **0 billing units**.

*Hypothetical boundary.* A supply end 29 days past the order date deducts no block; one 30 days past deducts exactly 1 block.
